newsletter.markdown:
1. **Discovery & Translational Science**

- **[Big Pharma]** **GSK highlights lung cancer data at WCLC26** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/14/biotech-news-gsk-touts-lung-data-from-two-drugs/)
  - Shared late-stage results for Definium's LSD treatment alongside comparative cross-trial analyses presented by discussants evaluating Arros-1 versus Trust I/II and Trident-1.
  - X/Twitter commentary from Jacob Plieth noted the data favored GSK's asset over competing programs.

2. **Early Trials — Phase I–II**

- **[Big Pharma]** **Lilly details upcoming EASD26 pipeline readouts** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2099812650116894957)
  - Set to present Phase 2 data for eloraTZP, a triple-acting candidate combining the selective amylin receptor agonist eloralintide with the GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide.
  - Presentations will also cover new data for Foundayo and retatrutide.

3. **Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III**

- **[Biotech]** **Vera reports final Phase 3 ORIGIN 3 data for Trutakna in IgAN** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/15/vera-kidney-drug-trutakna-shows-strong-phase-3-results-igan/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - Trutakna met all prespecified primary and secondary endpoints, stabilizing estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and reducing the risk of death and kidney complications through two years.
  - The trial demonstrated placebo-adjusted eGFR and composite kidney disease progression benefits.

- **[Biotech]** **Summit and Akeso present HARMONi-2 overall survival data for ivonescimab** [Bio Pharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/summit-akeso-wclc-2026-ivonescimab-lung-cancer-survival/830318/)
  - In a Phase 3 trial in non-small cell lung cancer, the dual-acting PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab reduced the relative risk of death by 27% compared to Merck's Keytruda, with a median overall survival of 30.8 months versus 22.6 months.
  - Benefit was more pronounced in tumors expressing high levels of target proteins; the findings aim to address investor skepticism regarding the generalizability of earlier data generated in China.

- **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca frontline SERENA-4 trial misses primary endpoint** [Bio Pharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/astrazeneca-etcamah-first-line-breast-cancer-study-results/830266/)
  - The oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERED) Etcamah, combined with standard therapy, failed to significantly delay progression compared to standard hormone therapy alone in newly diagnosed advanced ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.
  - Treatment yielded only a numerical improvement in progression-free survival that did not reach statistical significance.

4. **Regulatory & Approvals**

- **[Biotech]** **Vera plans sBLA submission for Trutakna** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2099809010237034574)
  - Following positive final Phase 3 ORIGIN 3 data in IgA nephropathy, the company plans to submit a supplemental Biologics License Application for full approval in the fourth quarter.

5. **Business & Strategy**

- **[Big Pharma]** **GSK acquires Chimagen Biosciences myeloma TCE asset** [X/Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2099791246726189371)
  - GSK entered into an agreement to acquire a T cell-engager for multiple myeloma from China-based biotech Chimagen Biosciences for up to $750 million.

- **[Biotech]** **Cellectis abandons CAR-T development for in vivo gene editing pivot** [Bio Pharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/cellectis-restructure-in-vivo-gene-editing-allogeneic-heart-disease/830281)
  - Cellectis is terminating clinical-stage donor-derived allogeneic CAR-T programs in leukemia and lymphoma due to material shifts in the commercial and clinical landscape, shifting resources to in vivo gene editing medicines.
  - The corporate restructuring triggered a stock drop of up to 43% in morning trading.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Abbott settles infant formula plant closure litigation** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/14/abbott-settlement-closure-baby-formula-plant-shortages/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - Abbott agreed to a $385 million settlement resolving claims tied to the 2022 shutdown of its major U.S. baby formula facility that triggered nationwide supply shortages.

6. **Public Health & Policy**

- **Federal judge blocks DHS visa restrictions for international scholars** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/14/court-halts-dhs-visa-limits-foreign-scholars/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - A federal judge halted an administration plan that sought to place a four-year cap on visas utilized by graduate students and post-doctoral researchers.

- **Pennsylvania reports third measles fatality** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/14/third-measles-related-death-pennsylvania-outbreak/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - State officials confirmed a Pennsylvania woman died from complications associated with measles, marking the state's third virus-related death this year.
